failure_modes: Compiling a temporal_teacher or temporal_region change would chase a sign-changing, sign-conflicting descriptive contrast (4-10 sign changes, 1-9 strong sign conflicts) and displace surrounding coordinates as noncore squared displacement, degrading the primary endpoint affinity objective.

Raising native_rms_ratio (C003) or time_ramp_power (C005/C006) without evidence of advantage would increase injection RMS beyond the already fully delivered ~0.33 calibration ratio, adding unnecessary coordinate displacement with no demonstrated affinity benefit.

Treating the large first/last rate z-values as a spatial gradient or as a validated monotone coordinate reward direction would misread a temporal derivative of coordinate features as a spatial gradient.
Presenting selection-node enrichment as final affinity benefit is unsupported because no decoded terminal labels are supplied (H002); last-record credit cannot substitute for final affinity.
rationale: D1.2: The registered time-conditioned alternatives are the temporal_teacher recipe ((1-blend)*R_static + blend*R_observed_teacher(time)) and the temporal_region recipe (same static teachers, validated absolute contrast changing regional attention at observed score nodes). Both change teacher coordinates/regional attention, not merely dose; the dose-only knobs are native_rms_ratio (C001-C003) and time_ramp_power (C004-C006), which are U-lane dose/ramp scalars. Analyst's temporal evidence (F003/F004, H001) shows the inspected continuous contrast features are observed-node coordinate contrasts with 4-10 sign changes and 1-9 strong sign conflicts, extrapolation disallowed, and whole-window z-values small and mixed in sign; this is descriptive, not a validated time-conditioned rule, and the first/last rate z-values are temporal derivatives of coordinate features, not spatial gradients and not a monotone coordinate reward direction. So no time-conditioned teacher-coordinate or regional-attention change is defensible, and the shared learned support (observed window [0.0,0.5], curve support [0.0,0.49], 50 observed score times) must be preserved. D4.1: Compared with the incumbent (native_rms_ratio 0.33, time_ramp_power 0.0, teacher_neighbors 4, teacher_score_beta 0, mixture_temperature 0.5, endpoint_pointcloud reward, FLOWR endpoint VJP), the offered choices are C001/C002/C003 (native_rms_ratio 0.2/0.33/0.5) and C004/C005/C006 (time_ramp_power 0.0/1.0/2.0). C002 and C004 are numerically identical to the incumbent, so they are not edits; C001/C003 change only dose magnitude and C005/C006 change only the U-lane ramp exponent, with no supplied evidence of a defensible expected affinity advantage. The delivery diagnostics show mean_delivered_over_calibration ~0.33 with zero backtrack, zero cap activation, zero noncore energy and zero post-window injection, i.e. the incumbent dose is already delivered as requested, so there is no evidence-driven reason to move it. Retaining the incumbent is therefore the evidence-supported choice; the evidence changes the decision only in the sense that it removes the apparent justification for a time-conditioned or dose edit rather than supplying one. D4.2: Opposing evidence (sign-changing, sign-conflicting landmark contrasts; small mixed whole-window z; no decoded terminal labels, H002) predicts a concrete failure if a time-conditioned teacher or regional-attention edit were compiled: the attention/teacher blend would chase a sign-changing descriptive feature, injecting unnecessary displacement of surrounding coordinates (noncore squared displacement) and degrading the primary endpoint affinity objective, while validity/strain are only secondary. Because affinity is primary and coordinate graph changes alone are not a failure mechanism, the design avoids that displacement by keeping the static teacher, the shared learned support and the incumbent dose/ramp. No temperature edit is proposed; temperatures are immutable task parameters.
